articles.title: BIMSTEC Grid Interconnection: Operationalizing Cross-Border Energy Diplomacy
articles.summary: India accelerates the implementation of the BIMSTEC Energy Grid Interconnection to foster regional trade and renewable energy integration.
prelims: BIMSTEC was established in 1997 through the Bangkok Declaration and is headquartered in Dhaka, Bangladesh.
The BIMSTEC Grid Interconnection Agreement facilitates cross-border electricity trade and grid integration among member nations.
Member countries include five from South Asia (Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Nepal, Sri Lanka) and two from Southeast Asia (Myanmar, Thailand).
articles.mains: Use to analyze regional connectivity, Neighborhood First policy, and energy diplomacy in South Asia and the Bay of Bengal region.

articles.title: National Green Hydrogen Mission: Standard Operating Guidelines for Green Ammonia Hubs
articles.summary: The Ministry of New and Renewable Energy introduces comprehensive guidelines for developing green ammonia bunkering and port export infrastructure.
prelims: Green Hydrogen is produced via water electrolysis powered by renewable energy sources, resulting in zero direct carbon emissions.
Green Ammonia is synthesized by combining green hydrogen with nitrogen separated from atmospheric air.
Strategic Interventions for Green Hydrogen Transition (SIGHT) is a key financial component under the National Green Hydrogen Mission.
articles.mains: Relevant for answers on industrial decarbonization, energy transition, clean shipping, and achieving India's Net-Zero by 2070 goal.

articles.title: GLOF Risk Mitigation: Deployment of Early Warning Systems in High-Altitude Himalayan Lakes
articles.summary: The National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA) initiates the installation of automated weather and water-level sensor networks across vulnerable glacial lakes.
prelims: Glacial Lake Outburst Floods (GLOFs) occur when a natural moraine or ice dam containing a glacial lake collapses rapidly.
South Lhonak Lake (Sikkim) and Lake Moriri (Ladakh) are prominent high-risk glacial lakes being monitored under the national framework.
The NDMA is the apex statutory body for disaster management in India, established under the Disaster Management Act, 2005, and chaired by the Prime Minister.
articles.mains: Directly applicable to questions on climate change adaptation, fragile Himalayan ecology, and proactive disaster risk reduction (DRR).

articles.title: Digital Public Infrastructure in Agriculture: Scale-Up of AgriStack Registry Framework
articles.summary: The Union Government expands the AgriStack platform to enable seamless digital credit access, crop insurance, and target subsidies for smallholder farmers.
prelims: AgriStack is a Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) incorporating three core registries: Farmers' Registry, Geo-referenced Village Maps, and Crop Sown Registry.
Each farmer is assigned a unique digital identity (Farmer ID) linked to land records for verification.
The project is implemented by the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare in collaboration with state land revenue departments.
articles.mains: Useful for topics on e-governance, administrative reforms, agricultural credit reform, and leveraging DPI for welfare distribution.

articles.title: Ethical Framework for Artificial Intelligence in Public Service Delivery
articles.summary: NITI Aayog releases updated guidelines on algorithmic transparency, accountability, and mitigation of bias in AI-driven welfare distribution systems.
prelims: NITI Aayog's 'National Strategy for Artificial Intelligence' outlines the 'AI for All' vision emphasizing ethical AI development.
Algorithmic bias refers to systematic and unfair outcomes caused by biased training data or flawed model assumptions.
Core ethical AI principles include Transparency, Explainability, Non-discrimination, Data Privacy, and Human Oversight.
articles.mains: Serves as standard reference material for GS4 Ethics questions on technology ethics, public accountability, administrative fairness, and digital governance.
